fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. "The cornerstone will come from Judah…" The LORD also says the tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler come from him. Judah is the house the LORD just said He attends to like a flock. That's a whole lot coming out of one house.

Yes, baker. "Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD." The gladness isn't kept to one generation. The kids get to watch it happen, and I think that's a gift for the whole family.
That's it, baker. "I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them." The people come back in such numbers that space runs out. That's a good problem to have.

Right, baker. "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." Assyria's pride comes down and Egypt's scepter leaves. Those two names come up again after the LORD said He'd gather His people from Assyria and bring them back from Egypt.

The message says, "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime…" He's the One who makes the storm clouds, and He will give everyone showers of rain and crops in the field. Friend, that's asking the owner of the oven about the oven.

Priests aren't in this verse at all, baker. The verse says, "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime…" The One to ask is the One who makes the storm clouds. He's also the One who will give showers of rain and crops in the field.
No lion here, friend. The LORD says He will make them "…like His royal steed in battle." That's a steed that belongs to Him, and it's a royal one. Lions and forests never come up in this verse.

No eagle in this verse, baker. The LORD "…will make them like His royal steed in battle." An eagle would be circling over the fight, but a steed is IN it. I think that's the whole point of the picture.
True, baker. The text says, "They will fight because the LORD is with them…" The reason is right there in the verse: He is with them. And the same verse says they will put the horsemen to shame.
That's the reason He gives: "I will restore them because I have compassion on them…" He tells them what He'll do, and He tells them why. Compassion is the whole answer, baker.

It's actually true, baker. The LORD says, "For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them." He promises to answer, right there in the verse. A promise that plain is one you read twice, just to enjoy it.

The verse says the opposite, baker. "Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands…" Folks forget where they left their keys in the very next room. These people remember Him from distant lands.

The verse doesn't say that, baker. It says, "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." No repenting and no bowing. Pride coming down and a scepter walking away is a quiet exit, with no apology speech in sight.

Not in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." Nobody joins and no gates open. Assyria isn't signing up for anything here. Its pride is coming down.
